subject: Mixed-mode streaming & batch throughput — post-call handback (Flightpath AI)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@flightpath.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 15:05:00 -0000
Subject: Mixed-mode streaming & batch throughput — post-call handback (Flightpath AI)

Alex / Jordan — thanks again for the sync. Quick recap and a proposed path forward so we can size Dedicated capacity and validate SLOs: 

Key takeaways from today's call:
- Two primary workloads: (A) interactive streaming chat for end-users (live agent augmentation), and (B) periodic batch enrichment jobs that run at predictable windows. Both share the same models but different patterns.
- Streaming requirements: sub-200ms initial token latency target for UX; steady per-chunk P95 < 80ms.
- Batch requirements: high crest capacity during weekly enrichment windows (~3–5 minutes) with larger response sizes.
- Current rough metrics (you provided): steady interactive concurrency ~420 connections, each ≈ 3 tokens/sec average when idle, spikes to ~20 tok/s during typing bursts. Baseline interactive QPS ≈ 15; peak interactive crest up to 240 QPS for 60–180s. Batch jobs: baseline 0.1 QPS but crest up to 140 QPS for short windows with avg tokens/request ~900.

Immediate sizing asks (what we need from you):
1) A small sample (csv) with 48 hours of real traffic: timestamp, flow_type (streaming|batch), tokens_in, tokens_out, request_duration_ms, connection_id. We attached a template (flightpath_workload_sample.csv).
2) Confirm maximum sustainable connection count during peak business hours (you mentioned 600 as an upper bound).
3) Any hard latency SLOs (P50/P95/P99) you must hit for the interactive flow.

Redwood proposal (high level):
- Target SLOs to design around: interactive initial-token P95 <= 180ms, per-chunk P95 <= 75ms; batch P95 <= 800ms for serialized responses.
- Baseline capacity recommendation (initial pilot): reserve capacity sized for steady tokens/sec ~10k and burst capacity to absorb crest tokens/sec up to ~200k for short windows using pre-warmed burst nodes / autoscale.
- We will run a smoke test: replay your 48h sample onto a staging cluster to validate tail latencies and memory/KV cache footprint.

Next steps I propose:
- You upload the sample CSV to the shared Drive link (or reply with the file).
- We'll schedule a 60-minute sizing session with Aditya (SRE/SE) and Marissa (CS) to walk through the data and finalize node counts. Proposed window: Thu 11 Mar 10:00–11:00 PT.

Attachments: flightpath_workload_sample.csv (template), SLO playbook stub (slo_playbook_for_fp.pdf).

—
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0197

From: Alex Moreno <alex@flightpath.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.ops@flightpath.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 18:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Mixed-mode streaming & batch throughput — post-call handback (Flightpath AI)

Thanks Soojin — that summary is great and aligns with what we discussed. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The 420 concurrent number is steady-state for our west-coast region; global peak could be ~620 if we include EU users during overlap windows.
- The batch crest numbers I gave are for our enrichment pipeline (one ingest job) — there can be up to 3 overlapping jobs occasionally (rare), so you should assume a conservative worst-case of 3x.

We'll upload a 48-hour sample into the Drive by EOD Thursday. Can confirm that Thu 11 Mar 10:00 PT works for the session (Aditya & Marissa ok?).

Two asks from our engineering lead:
1) When you say "burst nodes / autoscale" — can you call out whether those will be warm (preloaded model weights) or cold? Warm is preferred for the interactive flow.
2) What telemetry fields do you need in the CSV beyond the template? We can add extra columns if that helps with kernel-selection and KV cache sizing.

—
Alex Moreno
Head of Platform Engineering, Flightpath AI
alex@flightpath.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@flightpath.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 02:10:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Mixed-mode streaming & batch throughput — post-call handback (Flightpath AI)

Alex — quick answers:
- Burst nodes: for the interactive flow we'll use warm preloaded instances (weights in-GPU memory) for the pilot. For very large batch crests we may rely on a mix of warm + short-start burst nodes; we'll lay out a warm-count vs cost tradeoff once we see the sample.
- CSV telemetry: please include: request_id, timestamp_iso, flow_type, tokens_in, tokens_out, response_size_bytes, request_latency_ms (end-to-end), kv_cache_hit_ratio (if available), client_region, connection_duration_s. Extra useful but optional: avg_chunk_tokens and streaming_chunk_intervals_ms.

I'll put together a quick sizing worksheet after we get the sample and run a 24-hour replay in our staging. For the first pass I'd like to validate: steady tokens/sec, peak tokens/sec by 1-minute windows, and concurrent streaming connection memory footprint (KV size).

Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@flightpath.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Mixed-mode streaming & batch throughput — post-call handback (Flightpath AI)

Alex — thanks and great to meet you yesterday. Confirming Thu 11 Mar 10:00 PT (we've booked a room and a calendar invite with dial-in is on the way).

Two operational notes that will shape the pilot: 
- Canary strategy: we'll run a canary traffic split (5–10%) against a dedicated pool sized for your steady-state, then exercise incremental bursts up to your projected crest. This will exercise autoscaler and cache warm paths without exposing 100% of traffic.
- Observability: include a mapping from request_id -> user_id in the sample if you can (can be hashed/anonymized). That lets us correlate tail latencies to per-user session state during replay.

I'll also attach a short SLO appendix to the meeting invite (slo_playbook_for_fp.pdf) that proposes guardrails for initial SLAs and escalation paths. See you all Thu morning.

—
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
